note: attend_keys's development on the RTX 4090 machine (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 16 OpenMP workers), 20 October 2026: tests/test_mimo_attention.c's bench mode, Pro's full-layer shape (128 heads, 8 key/value heads, dims 192 and 128), ms a call, every variant's outputs the bytes of attend_heads'. 'heads' is attend_heads (the loop r3 runs), 'keys' attend_keys. The phases' times are thread 0's between the barriers (a scratch build with timers). Single runs vary by 5-10%.

exp_f8.check: tests/exp_f_check.c, -O3 -march=x86-64-v3: exp_f8 against exp_f on all 4294967296 floats, 0 differ, 731 handed to exp_f (its two roundings disagree; NaNs aside)

libgomp_team_small.note: the test linked with libgomp's team (a barrier about 60 us): attend_keys's four barriers cost it below 256 keys

spinning_team.note: linked with omp_spin.c as mimo.exe is

first_version.reading: One row's scores read the keys at about 63 GB/s (154 MB in 2.46 ms), the memory's pace; more workers stop helping past 16. For three rows the scores array (12.8 MB a row) is written, read and rewritten twice in the softmax and read once for each of a key head's four value parts: with the keys and values, about 640 MB a call, near what the memory gives in 9-10 ms.

value_parts_of_64_columns_24960_keys.note: 16 tasks: the weights read twice instead of four times, but a block's values and weights (16 KB + 12 KB) no longer fit the L1

scores_by_groups_of_eight_heads.layout: scores [row][key head][group of 8 heads][key][8]: a softmax task's 25,000 keys are one 800 KB stretch, in its core's L2 for its second pass

weights_divided_in_the_values_phase.note: the softmax one pass (exps and denominator), each value part dividing its block's exps into an L1 buffer: one pass over the scores less, the divisions four times over

value_parts_and_blocks.note: slices of 8 columns a part, keys a block

threshold: MIMO_ATTN_KEYS=128: with the spinning team attend_keys is the faster from 128 keys for one to three rows (at 64 keys and three rows the two are even); shorter contexts keep attend_heads, and so do the sliding-window layers (128 keys) whatever the context
